newsitem.title: UK: Joint venture company to run BBC finance services.
newsitem.headline: Joint venture company to run BBC finance services.

text.p: A joint venture company set up by Coopers & Lybrand and Electronic Data Systems will take charge of the BBC's financial management, the BBC said in a statement on Monday.
The BBC said it had signed a 10-year contract with Media Accounting Services Limited, the joint venture company, to streamline finance and business systems across the Corporation.
The new company will redesign the BBC's finance processes, seeking standardisation where possible, and create a single shared financial system and service, the BBC said.
"This contract lays the foundation for the BBC's aim of greater business efficiency and improved financial information in the digital age," said BBC Deputy Finance Director John Smith.

"There is a significant task ahead of us but the result will be the best possible finance system for the BBC and its staff, and substantial savings will be ploughed back into programmes and services for licence payers," he added.
The contract involves the transfer of existing BBC financial systems and around 90 related IT staff to Media Accounting Services on March 1.

The BBC and its partner will review the initial phase of the business process redesign late this year. If successful, finance staff will be transferred in early 1998 after a decision to proceed with building and implementation of the new system.
The BBC has a total of around 900 finance staff.
Coopers & Lybrand is one of the world's leading suppliers of services such as accounting and auditing, tax and consulting.
EDS, which employs some 98,000 people worldwide, is a leader in the global information services industry.

The BBC said it did not expect any redundancies as a result of the change. But it stressed that it was difficult at this stage to say exactly how many staff would be transferring to Media Accounting Services.
